newsitem.title: USA: CME says CFTC approves rise in milk contract size.
newsitem.headline: CME says CFTC approves rise in milk contract size.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange said the Commodity Futures Trading Commission has approved an increase in the size of the Fluid Milk contract to 200,000 lbs from 50,000 lbs.
The change will apply to all newly listed contract months beginning with the June 1997 contract to be listed for trading on Monday, October 7, 1996, CME said in a pess release.
In addition, the minimum price fluctuation will be reduced to $.01 per cwt ($20 per contract) from the previous $0.25 per cwt and deliveries will be allowed to be scheduled over a 4-day period.

Industry sources noted that the CME had requested the changes to meet changes occuring in the industry. Dairy co-ops will be doing forward contracting for their members and larger co-ops will have one to two million lbs of milk booked per day they will need to hedge to reduce risk. Also, the amount of contracts needed to spread between milk and butter futures contracts were much too wide due to the small milk contracts.
